causal-factors.name: Momentum from multiple 1B titles in 2025–2026
causal-factors.rationale: Lilo & Stitch, Zootopia 2, and Avatar: Fire and Ash have already crossed $1B worldwide by early 2026, establishing a proven track record that raises the odds of at least one new film hitting $1B by May 1, 2026.

causal-factors.name: Franchise/tentpole heavy release slate
causal-factors.rationale: A slate dominated by high-profile franchises (e.g., Avatar, Zootopia, Lilo & Stitch) elevates the probability that at least one film attains $1B worldwide.

causal-factors.name: China-market exposure and risk
causal-factors.rationale: China's market performance has been a key driver for some 1B titles; regulatory or demand shifts could dampen the overall probability.

causal-factors.name: Calendar-year timing advantage (early-year 1B hits seen in 2025–2026)
causal-factors.rationale: Early 1B successes in the current trend reduce the chance that no film hits $1B by May 1, 2026, though the effect is modest.

causal-factors.name: Recent 1B milestones by multiple titles in 2025-2026
causal-factors.rationale: By January 4, 2026, Avatar: Fire and Ash, Lilo & Stitch, and Zootopia 2 had already crossed $1B worldwide, showing the milestone is achievable early in the year and is becoming more common.

causal-factors.name: Large, forecasted 2026 global box office and dense franchise slate
causal-factors.rationale: Forecasts project global box office around $35B in 2026, driven by a calendar packed with franchises (Avengers, Spider-Man, Star Wars, etc.), which increases the odds of at least one $1B title by May 1, 2026.

causal-factors.name: Non-Hollywood 1B precedent (Ne Zha 2) expands the club
causal-factors.rationale: Ne Zha 2 achieved $1B in a single market (China) in 2025, signaling that non-Hollywood films can reach the milestone and broadening the pool of potential $1B titles.

causal-factors.name: China market regulatory risk for US releases
causal-factors.rationale: Tariff-related and regulatory restrictions on Hollywood films in China could dampen access to one of the largest potential markets, tempering the pace at which a film reaches $1B worldwide.

causal-factors.name: Streaming/cinema cannibalization risk
causal-factors.rationale: Growing streaming options and changing consumer habits could dampen theatrical attendance, constraining box-office totals despite a strong slate.

causal-factors.name: Strong 2025 1B year trail
causal-factors.rationale: Multiple films crossed $1B worldwide in 2025, indicating a durable market capable of hitting the milestone.

causal-factors.name: Early 2026 1B milestones achieved
causal-factors.rationale: Avatar: Fire and Ash and other titles reached $1B by January 2026, sustaining momentum toward May 1.

causal-factors.name: Franchise-heavy 2026 slate
causal-factors.rationale: Forecasts project a ~$35B global year driven by franchises, increasing odds of at least one $1B release.

causal-factors.name: China-market risk in 2026
causal-factors.rationale: China-market dynamics and potential restrictions could dampen global grosses and reduce likelihood of a 1B title within the window.

causal-factors.name: Release-schedule risk (potential delays)
causal-factors.rationale: Potential schedule shifts could push the milestone beyond May 1, especially if key titles slip.

synthesis: The threshold has clearly been breached by early 2026, with multiple 1B titles, supporting near-certainty that at least one film will surpass $1B before May 1, 2026. While headwinds exist, they are not sufficient to undermine the milestone achieved, justifying a modest calibration upward from the ensemble.
